text:
The percentage of all product customers with an export problem cannot be determined from this log. The total customer population is missing, and this small helpdesk sample does not represent all customers.

The complete one-week log contains five occurrences across three distinct events and three customers:

| Wording group | Entries | Occurrences | Distinct events | Cause |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| Export failed | E1, E2, E3 | 3 | 1: X, customer A | Unknown |
| Login failed | E4 | 1 | 1: Y, customer B | Unknown |
| Display failed | E5 | 1 | 1: Z, customer C | Unknown |

E1–E3 are repeated reports of the same unresolved event, not three independent export failures. This is an isolated export signal, not a demonstrated pattern across distinct instances. Confidence is high because the log explicitly identifies the same event.

Grouping by underlying cause is not possible: no diagnoses or supporting diagnostic evidence are recorded. The shared word “failed” does not establish a common cause across export, login and display issues. Confidence in any recurring-cause claim is low.

A person should verify the diagnoses and review whether any finding warrants action. Answering the customer-percentage question would additionally require a defined measurement period, the total customer population and reliable customer-level evidence of export problems. No fix or process change is established by this log.
